variants.headline: New settlers land from the ship
variants.sub: The ship in port has brought new settlers who landed at {district}.
variants.body:
New settlers have landed from the ship at {district}. The number arriving is {migrants}. Their arrival is an entry into the colony, not a complete account of the lives that follow. For {target}, the relevant question concerns responsibility towards newcomers as people rather than merely an addition to a count.

Off the ship and into a new chapter. It is an attractive phrase; the people arriving deserve more than a phrase. Readers can recognise the human meaning of a landing without being given a fictional reunion, a perfect job or a promise that beginning again is automatically easy.

We judge {target} critically. A landing should not place the treatment of newcomers beyond question; people joining the colony deserve a more serious standard than a welcoming description with practical responsibility left outside it. Readers deserve a clear story and a straight answer about responsibility.
